query: When was the palace founded at which Columba de Dunbar died in 1435?

pipeline_result.response: The palace was founded at Broadclyst in Devon, England, by Bishop Columba de Dunbar from 1422 until his death in 1435.
retrieved_context: Columba de Dunbar: Columba de Dunbar ( 1386 – 1435) was Bishop of Moray from 1422 until his death at Spynie Palace near Elgin sometime before 7 November 1435.

Buckingham Palace: Buckingham Palace ( ) is the London residence and administrative headquarters of the reigning monarch of the United Kingdom.  Located in the City of Westminster, the palace is often at the centre of state occasions and royal hospitality.  It has been a focal point for the British people at times of national rejoicing and mourning.

Columbjohn: Columb John (today "Columbjohn") in the parish of Broadclyst in Devon, England, is an historic estate and was briefly the seat of the prominent Acland family which later moved to the adjacent estate of Killerton.  Nothing of the structure of the Acland mansion house survives except the arch to the gatehouse, dated about 1590, and the private chapel, restored in 1851.  The site of the former mansion house is situated one mile due west of Killerton House, and five miles north-east of the historic centre of the City of Exeter.  The estate's name derives from it having been held by the Culme family, whose own name was taken from its landholdings in the vicinity of the River Culm, which flows through the Columb John estate.
